# Adjudication Task — Chapter 206

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃206화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|띠링.
  6|
  7|
  8|
  9|- [로그아웃]을 완료했습니다.
 10|
 11|
 12|
 13|눈을 뜨지 않았지만 알 수 있었다.
 14|
 15|시스템 알림과 동시에 나를 둘러싼 모든 것이 바뀌었음을.
 16|
 17|털가죽이 깔린 침상과 딱딱한 목침 대신 푹신한 소파의 쿠션이 느껴졌고, 보글보글 물 끓는 소리와 함께 익숙한 냄새가 코를 찔렀다.
 18|
 19|‘이, 이건…….’
 20|
 21|라면 냄새다. 그것도 끝내주게 잘 끓인!
 22|
 23|깨닫자마자 무림에서 한 달이 넘는 시간을 보내며 조미료를 갈구하던 위장이 격렬하게 요동쳤다.
 24|
 25|“배고파!”
 26|
 27|영혼을 실은 외침과 함께 번쩍 눈을 뜨자 환하게 불이 켜진 부엌에서 낯익은 얼굴이 쏙 삐져나왔다.
 28|
 29|드문드문 난 턱수염과 떡 진 머리. 김이 잔뜩 서린 안경알을 문지른 진호 형이 활짝 웃는다.
 30|
 31|“오오, 사랑하는 내 동생 태경이. 잘 잤니?”
 32|
 33|평소와는 다른 역겨운 말투였지만 나는 이미 라면 냄새를 맡고 눈이 뒤집힌 상태였다.
 34|
 35|“라면!”
 36|
 37|“깜짝이야, 왜 이래?”
 38|
 39|“김치!”
 40|
 41|“너 진짜 잘 자더라. 흔들어서 깨우려고 했는데.”
 42|
 43|“찬밥! 최소 다섯 공기!”
 44|
 45|“……어, 알았다. 안 그래도 지금 가져가려고 했어.”
 46|
 47|잠시 후, 냄비 한가득 채워진 국물과 면발을 마주한 나는 황홀한 목소리로 중얼거렸다.
 48|
 49|“미쳤다…….”
 50|
 51|“면발 윗부분만 살짝 올려봐. 안에 반숙 있다.”
 52|
 53|“헉.”
 54|
 55|과연 그 말대로다. 살살 면발을 걷어 올리자 완벽한 형태를 유지한 반숙 계란이 모습을 드러냈다.
 56|
 57|헛숨을 삼키는 내게 진호 형이 작은 앞접시 두 개를 내밀었다.
 58|
 59|“자, 여기 김치랑 단무지. 밥은 한 시간 전에 꺼내 놓은 흰쌀밥. 면발 다 건져 먹고 국물 몇 모금 마신 다음에 찬밥을 투하하면…….”
 60|
 61|“당신은.”
 62|
 63|“응?”
 64|
 65|“당신은 신입니까?”
 66|
 67|진호 형이 고시 참고서를 냄비 밑에 깔며 엄숙하게 대답했다.
 68|
 69|“창세기서 1장 1절. 성진호 가로되, 지금 먹지 않으면 국물은 식고 면발은 불어 터지리라.”
 70|
 71|“앗, 아아.”
 72|
 73|“어린 양아, 어찌 라면을 앞에 두고 주둥이를 놀리느냐. 국물 한 방울 남기지 말고 싹싹 핥아먹거라.”
 74|
 75|평생을 무교로 살았지만 이제는 아니다.
 76|
 77|나는 진호 형을 우러러보며 젓가락을 들었다.
 78|
 79|“아멘.”
 80|
 81|“라멘.”
 82|
 83|오늘만큼은 라면 국물에 코를 박고 죽어도 좋아.
 84|
 85|커다란 냄비에 고개를 처박고 쉴 새 없이 젓가락을 놀렸다. 입과 젓가락의 동선이 짧으니 면발이 끊임없이 들어간다.
 86|
 87|후룩! 후루룩! 후루루루룩!
 88|
 89|탱탱한 면발, 얼큰한 국물. 반숙 계란을 터트릴 때는 황홀함과 안타까움을 참지 못하고 눈물 한 방울이 또르륵 흘러내렸다.
 90|
 91|‘맛있다. 너무 맛있어.’
 92|
 93|조미료 좋아. 최고야.
 94|
 95|오직 현대에서만 맛볼 수 있는 인공적인 맛에 취해 흡입하기를 한참.
 96|
 97|문득 정신을 차려 보니 눈앞엔 텅 빈 냄비와 그릇들뿐이었다. 찬밥이 고봉밥처럼 수북이 남겨 있던 그릇까지 깨끗했다.
 98|
 99|“꺼윽.”
100|
101|“이런 미친.”
102|
103|거하게 트림하며 배를 문지르는 나를 진호 형이 질린 눈빛으로 바라봤다.
104|
105|“라면 일곱 봉지에 밥 다섯 공기를 10분 만에 혼자 먹어? 너 사람 맞냐?”
106|
107|“탄산! 콜라!”
108|
109|“……지, 진정해라. 갖고 올게.”
110|
111|결국 1.5L짜리 콜라를 연이어 세 개나 비운 후에야 어느 정도 정신이 돌아왔다.
112|
113|“휴, 잘 먹었다. 배불러.”
114|
115|“그거 이상하네. 난 왜 배가 고프지.”
116|
117|“참아. 형이 나였어도 그랬을 거야.”
118|
119|대충 대답하고 뒤에 놓인 소파에 쓰러지듯 등을 기댔다.
120|
121|이게 무슨 몬스터의 가죽으로 만든 거라고 했었나? 그래서인지 촉감이 아주 일품이다.
122|
123|“어이고, 편하다.”
124|
125|고시원 원룸이었으면 소파 들어갈 자리도 없었을 거다.
126|
127|진호 형도 부엌이 아니라 공용 휴게실에서 라면을 끓이거나 버너를 가져와야 했겠지.
128|
129|“역시 이사 오길 잘했어.”
130|
131|진호 형이 숟가락으로 냄비 바닥을 긁으며 대답했다.
132|
133|“그러게. 집 좋더라.”
134|
135|“그치? 나중에 엄마나 하연이가 보면 얼마나 좋아할……지.”
136|
137|순간 뇌리를 스치는 섬광 같은 깨달음.
138|
139|나는 멍하니 입을 벌린 채 주위를 둘러봤다. 고시원과는 비교도 안 될 정도로 넓은 공간과 가구.
140|
141|그리고 이 공간과 상황에 자연스럽게 녹아든 한 사람.
142|
143|“배고프다. 짜파게티나 더 끓일까.”
144|
145|“…….”
146|
147|“이번엔 안 준다. 먹을 거면 지금 딱 말해.”
148|
149|간신히 목소리를 쥐어짜 냈다.
150|
151|“……꺄.”
152|
153|“응?”
154|
155|“네가 왜 여기 있어. 이 새꺄!”
156|
157|아직 캄캄한 새벽, 터져 나온 포효가 일산 주택 단지를 뒤흔들었다.
158|
159|
160|
161|* * *
162|
163|
164|
165|전후 사정을 모두 들은 나는 기가 차 되물을 수밖에 없었다.
166|
167|“캡슐 안에 있었다고?”
168|
169|공손히 무릎을 꿇고 두 팔을 번쩍 든 진호 형이 시선을 피하며 대답했다.
170|
171|“응. 숨 꾹 참고 가만히 있었지.”
172|
173|어쩐지 이삿짐센터 아저씨가 쩔쩔매더라니.
174|
175|나조차도 별 위화감을 느끼지 못했다. 맨 처음 캡슐을 발견해서 옮겼을 때와 비교해 근력이 몇 배는 강해졌을뿐더러 그땐 지금처럼 기감이 뛰어나지도 않았기 때문이다.
176|
177|그리고 한 가지 더.
178|
179|‘아니 시바, 그걸 누가 상상이나 했겠냐고.’
180|
181|아무리 비싸고 뛰어난 경보 시스템이 있어도 전원이 꺼져 있으면 침입을 알 수 없는 법.
182|
183|설마 캡슐 안에 사람이 숨어 있었을 줄은 전혀 예상하지 못했다.
184|
185|“후우. 구한다던 집은 어쩌고? 친구랑 같이 방 구해서 나간다고 하지 않았어?”
186|
187|“그, 김종수 알지? 내 대학교 동문. 재작년쯤에 너도 껴서 같이 술도 한잔했잖아.”
188|
189|얼굴은 가물가물하지만 확실히 그랬던 기억이 있다.
190|
191|당시에는 제법 잘나가는 중고차 딜러라고 했던가? 그날 소고기를 사 주지 않았다면 그런 기억도 진작 잊었을 것이다.
192|
193|“같이 산다던 친구가 그 사람이야?”
194|
195|“맞아. 이제 친구는 아니지만.”
196|
197|“형 혹시…….”
198|
199|“보증금 오백. 그 새끼가 먹고 날랐다.”
200|
201|왜 안 좋은 예감은 늘 적중하는 걸까.
202|
203|나는 지끈거리는 이마를 문질렀다.
204|
205|“어쩌다가?”
206|
207|“그게, 내가 얼마 후면 시험이니까 세부적인 일은 자기가 처리하겠다고…….”
208|
209|손을 들어 이어지려는 말을 막았다.
210|
211|나머지는 안 들어봐도 뻔하다. 상투적이지만 늘 먹히는 방법의 하나니까.
212|
213|“아니, 그걸 제대로 알아보지도 않고 턱 맡긴 거야?”
214|
215|“10년을 넘게 알았는데 그깟 돈 몇백 때문에 그럴 줄 알았겠냐.”
216|
217|“하지만 그깟 돈 몇백이 형 전 재산인 거 아냐?”
218|
219|“…….”
220|
221|캡슐에 몰래 숨어서까지 들어왔을 정도면 이번 달에 낼 고시원 월세도 안 남았을 것이 분명하다.
222|
223|‘고향이 제주도인가.’
224|
225|특A급 흑우.
226|
227|흑우도 이런 흑우가 없다. 그런 내 눈빛에 진호 형이 고개를 푹 숙였다.
228|
229|“돈 마련할 때까지 두어 달만 신세 지려고 했어.”
230|
231|“차라리 나한테 말을 하지.”
232|
233|“혼자 고민도 많이 했는데 차마 입이 안 떨어지더라. 그래도 형이 돼서 동생한테 민폐를 끼칠 수는 없잖아.”
234|
235|“…….”
236|
237|아니, 이 인간은 민폐의 기준이 뭐야 도대체.
238|
239|“미안하다. 정말.”
240|
241|처연한 목소리와 함께 진호 형이 팔을 내렸다. 어느새 눈동자가 촉촉하게 젖어 있었다.
242|
243|“태경아…….”
244|
245|“진호 형…….”
246|
247|나는 측은한 목소리로 말을 이었다.
248|
249|“누가 팔 내리래.”
250|
251|“응?”
252|
253|“다시 손 들어. 처맞기 전에.”
254|
255|“……옙.”
256|
257|냉큼 팔을 원위치하는 진호 형의 모습에 절로 한숨이 흘러나왔다.
258|
259|생각지도 못했던 상황에 어이가 없기도 하고, 한편으로는 마음이 착잡했다.
260|
261|‘진작 말을 하지.’
262|
263|과거였다면 모를까, 지금의 나는 진호 형을 도와줄 여력이 충분하다. 아니, 설령 예전이라 하더라도 물심양면으로 도왔을 것이다.
264|
265|‘함께한 시간이 얼마인데.’
266|
267|피만 안 섞였지 친형제나 다름없는 사람. 그게 바로 진호 형이었다.
268|
269|그를 혼자 두고 떠나는 것이 마음에 걸려 잠깐이나마 같이 살자고 제의해 볼까 고민한 적도 있다.
270|
271|‘어차피 엄마나 하연이에게는 수능 끝난 후에 말할 계획이었으니까 시간이 좀 남아 있긴 한데…….’
272|
273|고민하는 눈빛으로 집 안을 둘러봤다. 어린 시절의 기억 속 모습과는 다르지만 마침내 되찾은 우리 가족의 집이다.
274|
275|이제는 목소리도 흐릿한 아버지의 흔적이 남아 있는 집.
276|
277|마침내 마음의 결정을 내린 내가 입을 열었다.
278|
279|“이 집은 안 되겠다, 형. 섭섭해도 이해해 줘.”
280|
281|진호 형이 애써 밝은 표정으로 고개를 저었다.
282|
283|“섭섭할 게 뭐가 있냐. 다 내 잘못인데.”
284|
285|“짐은? 풀어 놨어?”
286|
287|“아직. 어차피 책이랑 옷가지 몇 개가 전부라 가벼워. 너 출근할 때 같이 나가지, 뭐.”
288|
289|그러고 보니 아까부터 창밖이 환하다. 어느새 여덟 시다. 교통 체증이나 일산과 부천의 거리를 생각하면 출근 시간까지 제법 아슬아슬했다.
290|
291|“따로 가야 할 것 같은데? 일단 미리 챙겨 놔.”
292|
293|“그래, 알았다.”
294|
295|“그리고 나 퇴근하기 전까지 새집 청소도 싹 해 놓고.”
296|
297|“……응?”
298|
299|“오해하지 마, 여기 아니니까. 잠깐만.”
300|
301|나는 핸드폰을 꺼내 메신저를 뒤적거렸다.
302|
303|그리고 마침내 ‘명품충’으로 저장된 최 팀장과의 톡에서 찾고 있던 주소를 발견했다.
304|
305|“아, 여기 있다. 지금 형 번호로 주소 보냈으니까 알아서 찾아가.”
306|
307|“잠깐만. 무슨 주소?”
308|
309|“오피스텔.”
310|
311|“어?”
312|
313|“길드에서 지원해 준다고 했던 집 있거든. 지난번에는 부담스러워서 거절했었는데, 이참에 받지 뭐.”
314|
315|눈을 동그랗게 뜨는 진호 형을 보자 피식 웃음이 새어 나왔다.
316|
317|“뭘 그렇게 놀라. 나 요즘 잘나가.”
318|
319|“……!”
320|
321|“이 집도 리모델링 해야 하니까 거기서 같이 살자. 어차피 나야 출퇴근하기도 쉬워지니까 좋고.”
322|
323|“태, 태경아.”
324|
325|나는 진호 형의 떨리는 목소리를 못 들은 척 돌아섰다.
326|
327|아침부터 낯간지러운 장면은 사양이다. 내가 가장 힘들었던 시절 위로해 준 사람에게 굳이 감사하다는 말을 듣고 싶지도 않았다.
328|
329|‘됐어.’
330|
331|그래, 이거면 된 거다.
332|
333|
334|
335|* * *
336|
337|
338|

Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

[P161]
I had no desire to deal with an embarrassing scene first thing in the morning. Nor did I particularly want to be thanked by the man who had comforted me through the hardest period of my life.

[P162]
*It’s fine.*

[P163]
Yeah. This was enough.

[P164]
* * *

[P165]
It was mid-September. The worst of the heat had passed, but the morning commute hadn’t changed.

[P166]
The taxi driver leaned on his horn whenever some shameless driver tried to cut into the stalled traffic, then turned up the radio.

[P167]
> An F-rank Gate has appeared in Uldae-ri, Jangheung-myeon, Yangju City, prompting an immediate evacuation order. Nearby Hunters and military units are working together to suppress it, and six casualties have been confirmed so far…

[P168]
“Goddamn it. As if the traffic wasn’t bad enough, now those monster bastards are raising hell too.”

[P169]
After delivering the colorful curse, he glanced at me in the passenger seat.

[P170]
“You’re a Hunter too, right?”

[P171]
“For now.”

[P172]
At this point, I wasn’t entirely sure whether I was a Hunter or a Murim warrior.

[P173]
Officially, at least in the modern world, I was a C-rank Hunter with Hope Guild.

[P174]
The taxi driver grinned at my answer.

[P175]
“I knew it. You can always spot a Hunter.”

[P176]
“I suppose so.”

[P177]
It was like the difference between a herbivore and a carnivore.

[P178]
There were exceptions, but everyone gave off a certain air. Someone my size carrying a large case had to be one of two things:

[P179]
A musician who loved working out, or a Hunter.

[P180]
*You can tell at a glance.*

[P181]
It wasn’t anything particularly remarkable, especially for a taxi driver who met countless passengers every day.

[P182]
But this middle-aged man’s mouth never stopped moving.

[P183]
“Hey, can I ask you something?”

[P184]
“Sure.”

[P185]
“It feels like Gates have been opening more often lately. Can’t anything be done about that?”

[P186]
“……What?”

[P187]
“I mean, how are ordinary people like me supposed to live without worrying? I could wake up tomorrow morning and find a Gate in my apartment parking lot. I can work my ass off taking fares all day, but it’s not like I can afford property in a safe zone.”

[P188]
I stared at him incredulously.

[P189]
“That’s true, but why are you asking me?”

[P190]
“I know. I’m just frustrated, that’s all. Frustrated.”

[P191]
“……So am I.”

[P192]
I was a Hunter, not a prophet.

[P193]
How was I supposed to predict something even Nostradamus couldn’t?

[P194]
No one could predict when or where a Gate would form. The only reason early suppression was possible was because astronomical sums had been spent installing mana detectors everywhere.

[P195]
Just like the breaking news now coming over the radio.

[P196]
> Breaking news. The F-rank Gate reported earlier in Yangju City has been stabilized. Hunters and military forces have exterminated a total of fifty-eight goblins and are conducting a search for any remaining monsters…

[P197]
“Every time you turn around, it’s Gates and monsters. I’m sick to death of it.”

[P198]
Beep.

[P199]
The taxi driver switched off the radio with an irritated jab.

[P200]
An uncomfortable silence settled over the car, but I was more than happy to spend the rest of the trip in peace.

[P201]
*I wonder what Mom and Hayeon are doing right now.*

[P202]
I was gazing out the window, lost in thought, when it happened.

[P203]
Honk! Hoooonk!

[P204]
A faint blare pierced my ears, followed by a jumble of overlapping noises. I hurriedly rolled down the window.

[P205]
*What is that? Was there an accident?*

[P206]
The taxi driver stared at me in confusion.

[P207]
“Why are you opening the window when I’ve got the air conditioner on—”

[P208]
“Wait. Just give me a second.”

[P209]
My serious tone silenced him. I drew up my internal energy.

[P210]
My hearing and vision, already far beyond the limits of an ordinary human, swept across the congested road.

[P211]
“Huh?”

[P212]
Far in the distance, a black dot shot into the air.

[P213]
It began to fall in an arc, and I realized what it was.

[P214]
“……A car?”

[P215]
It had been crushed into a ball, but I could still see it clearly.

[P216]
The crumpled hood. The twisted metal.

[P217]
The shower of glass spilling from it as it hurtled toward us.

[P218]
And exactly where it was going to land.

[P219]
Whoooooosh!

[P220]
*Oh, shit.*

[P221]
Why here of all places?

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 206

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃206화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|띠링.
  6|
  7|
  8|
  9|- [로그아웃]을 완료했습니다.
 10|
 11|
 12|
 13|눈을 뜨지 않았지만 알 수 있었다.
 14|
 15|시스템 알림과 동시에 나를 둘러싼 모든 것이 바뀌었음을.
 16|
 17|털가죽이 깔린 침상과 딱딱한 목침 대신 푹신한 소파의 쿠션이 느껴졌고, 보글보글 물 끓는 소리와 함께 익숙한 냄새가 코를 찔렀다.
 18|
 19|‘이, 이건…….’
 20|
 21|라면 냄새다. 그것도 끝내주게 잘 끓인!
 22|
 23|깨닫자마자 무림에서 한 달이 넘는 시간을 보내며 조미료를 갈구하던 위장이 격렬하게 요동쳤다.
 24|
 25|“배고파!”
 26|
 27|영혼을 실은 외침과 함께 번쩍 눈을 뜨자 환하게 불이 켜진 부엌에서 낯익은 얼굴이 쏙 삐져나왔다.
 28|
 29|드문드문 난 턱수염과 떡 진 머리. 김이 잔뜩 서린 안경알을 문지른 진호 형이 활짝 웃는다.
 30|
 31|“오오, 사랑하는 내 동생 태경이. 잘 잤니?”
 32|
 33|평소와는 다른 역겨운 말투였지만 나는 이미 라면 냄새를 맡고 눈이 뒤집힌 상태였다.
 34|
 35|“라면!”
 36|
 37|“깜짝이야, 왜 이래?”
 38|
 39|“김치!”
 40|
 41|“너 진짜 잘 자더라. 흔들어서 깨우려고 했는데.”
 42|
 43|“찬밥! 최소 다섯 공기!”
 44|
 45|“……어, 알았다. 안 그래도 지금 가져가려고 했어.”
 46|
 47|잠시 후, 냄비 한가득 채워진 국물과 면발을 마주한 나는 황홀한 목소리로 중얼거렸다.
 48|
 49|“미쳤다…….”
 50|
 51|“면발 윗부분만 살짝 올려봐. 안에 반숙 있다.”
 52|

[P41]
I bent over the huge pot and worked my chopsticks without pause. With so little distance between the noodles and my mouth, they flowed into me without end.

[P42]
Slurp! Slurp! Slurrrrrp!

[P43]
Springy noodles. Spicy broth. When I broke open the soft-boiled egg, the bliss and regret were so overwhelming that a single tear rolled down my cheek.

[P44]
*It’s delicious. So delicious.*

[P45]
I love seasoning. It’s the best.

[P46]
Drunk on that artificial flavor found only in the modern world, I kept inhaling food.

[P47]
By the time I came to my senses, there was nothing in front of me but empty pots and bowls. Even the bowl that had held a heaping mound of cold rice was spotless.

[P48]
“Buuurp.”

[P49]
“You’ve got to be kidding me.”

[P50]
Jinho stared at me in horror as I rubbed my stomach and let out a tremendous belch.

[P51]
“You ate seven packets of ramen and five bowls of rice by yourself in ten minutes? Are you even human?”

[P52]
“Carbonation! Cola!”

[P53]
“……C-Calm down. I’ll get some.”

[P54]

[P55]
“Whew. That hit the spot. I’m full.”

[P56]
“That’s strange. Why am I hungry?”

[P57]
“Bear with it. You would’ve done the same if you were me.”

[P58]
I answered absently and collapsed back against the sofa behind me.

[P59]

[P60]
“Man, this is comfortable.”

[P61]
If this had been my goshiwon room,[^1] there wouldn’t even have been space for a sofa.

[P62]
Jinho would have had to cook the ramen in the communal lounge instead of a kitchen, or bring in a portable burner.

[P63]
“Moving here really was the right choice.”

[P64]
“Yeah. It’s a nice place.”

[P65]
Jinho scraped the bottom of the pot with a spoon as he answered.

[P66]
“Right? Mom and Hayeon are going to love it when they see… it.”

[P67]
A realization flashed through my mind like lightning.

[P68]
My mouth fell open as I stared around the room. It was incomparably larger than the goshiwon, and filled with furniture.

[P69]
And one particular person had blended seamlessly into both the space and the situation.

[P70]
“I’m still hungry. Should I make some Jjapagetti?”

[P71]
“……”

[P72]
“I’m not giving you any this time. If you want some, say so now.”

[P73]
I barely managed to squeeze out my voice.

[P74]
“……You.”

[P75]
“Hm?”

[P76]
“Why the hell are you here, you bastard!”

[P77]
My roar shattered the dark dawn and shook the residential neighborhood of Ilsan.

[P79]
After hearing the whole story, I could only ask in disbelief.

[P80]
“You were inside the capsule?”

[P81]
Jinho knelt politely with both arms raised above his head and looked away.

[P82]
“Yeah. I held my breath and stayed perfectly still.”

[P83]
No wonder the mover had struggled so much.

[P84]
Even I hadn’t noticed anything unusual. My Strength had grown several times over since I’d first found and moved the capsule, and my Qi Sense hadn’t been nearly as sharp back then as it was now.

[P85]
And there was one more thing.

[P86]
*No, for fuck’s sake. Who would’ve imagined that?*

[P87]
No matter how expensive or sophisticated an alarm system was, it couldn’t detect an intruder when the power was off.

[P88]
It had never even occurred to me that someone might be hiding inside the capsule.

[P89]
“Whew. What happened to the place you were going to get? Didn’t you say you were moving in with a friend?”

[P90]
“Y-You know Kim Jong-su, right? My college classmate. You had drinks with us once a couple of years ago.”

[P91]
His face was hazy in my memory, but I did remember that.

[P92]
Hadn’t he been a fairly successful used-car dealer at the time? If he hadn’t bought us beef that day, I probably would’ve forgotten him completely.

[P93]
“That’s the friend you were going to live with?”

[P94]
“Yeah. Though he’s not my friend anymore.”

[P95]
“Hyung, did he…?”

[P96]
“Five million won for the deposit. That bastard took it and ran.”

[P97]
Why did bad premonitions always come true?

[P98]
I rubbed my throbbing forehead.

[P99]
“How did that happen?”

[P100]
“Well, my exam is coming up soon, so he said he’d handle all the details…”

[P101]
I raised a hand to stop him.

[P102]
I didn’t need to hear the rest. It was a clichéd trick, but it kept working for a reason.

[P103]
“You just handed him the money without checking anything?”

[P104]
“I’d known him for over ten years. How was I supposed to know he’d do that over a few million won?”

[P105]
“But those few million won were your entire fortune, weren’t they?”

[P106]
“……”

[P107]
If he’d gone so far as to sneak in here inside the capsule, he clearly didn’t even have enough left to pay this month’s goshiwon rent.

[P108]
*Was he from Jeju Island or something?*

[P109]
A special A-grade black cow.[^2]

[P110]
There wasn’t a bigger sucker alive.

[P111]
At the look in my eyes, Jinho hung his head.

[P112]
“I was only going to impose on you for a couple of months, until I could scrape some money together.”

[P113]
“You should’ve just told me.”

[P114]
“I agonized over it, but I couldn’t bring myself to say anything. I’m your hyung. I can’t burden my little brother.”

[P115]
“……”

[P116]
What the hell did this man consider a burden?

[P117]
“I’m sorry. I really am.”

[P118]
His voice turned mournful as he lowered his arms. His eyes were already glistening.

[P119]
“Taekyung…”

[P120]
“Jinho hyung…”

[P121]
I continued in a sympathetic voice.

[P122]
“Who told you to lower your arms?”

[P123]
“Hm?”

[P124]
“Put them back up before I beat you.”

[P125]
“……Yes, sir.”

[P126]
Jinho hurriedly raised his arms again, and a sigh escaped me.

[P127]
The whole ridiculous situation had come out of nowhere, but at the same time, it left me feeling heavyhearted.

[P128]
*You should’ve told me sooner.*

[P129]
Maybe I couldn’t have done much for him in the past, but now I had more than enough means to help. No, even back then, I would’ve supported him in every way I could.

[P130]
*After all the time we’ve spent together.*

[P131]
We weren’t related by blood, but he was as good as a real brother to me. That was who Jinho was.

[P132]
I’d even considered asking him to live with me for a while because I felt uneasy about leaving him on his own.

[P133]
*I was planning to tell Mom and Hayeon after the college entrance exam anyway, so there’s still some time, but…*

[P134]
I looked around the house, deep in thought. It looked different from the home in my childhood memories, but it was still the house my family had finally reclaimed.

[P135]
A house that still held traces of my father, whose voice had faded in my memory.

[P136]
At last, I made up my mind.

[P137]
“This house won’t work, hyung. I know you’ll be disappointed, but try to understand.”

[P138]
Jinho forced a bright expression and shook his head.

[P139]
“Why would I be disappointed? This is all my fault.”

[P140]
“What about your stuff? Have you unpacked?”

[P141]
“Not yet. It’s only a few books and some clothes, so there isn’t much. I’ll just leave with you when you go to work.”

[P142]
Come to think of it, it had been bright outside for a while. It was already eight o’clock. Between the traffic and the distance from Ilsan to Bucheon, I was cutting it pretty close.

[P143]
“I think we’ll have to leave separately. Get your things ready.”

[P144]
“Okay.”

[P145]
“And clean the new place from top to bottom before I get off work.”

[P146]
“……Huh?”

[P147]
“Don’t get the wrong idea. I’m not talking about this house. Give me a second.”

[P148]
I pulled out my phone and searched through my messages.

[P149]
At last, I found the address I wanted in my chat with Team Leader Choi, whom I’d saved as “Designer-Brand Junkie.”

[P150]
“Ah, here it is. I just sent the address to your phone. Find your own way there.”

[P151]
“Wait. What address?”

[P152]
“An officetel.”

[P153]
“Huh?”

[P154]
“The Guild offered to provide me with a place. I turned it down last time because accepting it felt like too much, but I might as well take them up on it now.”

[P155]
A quiet laugh escaped me when I saw Jinho’s eyes widen.

[P156]
“Why are you so surprised? I’m doing pretty well these days.”

[P157]
“……!”

[P158]
“This house needs remodeling anyway, so let’s live there together. It’ll make my commute easier too.”

[P159]
“Ta-Taekyung.”

[P160]
I turned away, pretending not to hear the tremor in Jinho’s voice.

[P161]
I had no desire to deal with an embarrassing scene first thing in the morning. Nor did I particularly want to be thanked by the man who had comforted me through the hardest period of my life.

[P162]
*It’s fine.*

[P163]
Yeah. This was enough.

[P165]
It was mid-September. The worst of the heat had passed, but the morning commute hadn’t changed.

[P166]
The taxi driver leaned on his horn whenever some shameless driver tried to cut into the stalled traffic, then turned up the radio.

[P167]
> An F-rank Gate has appeared in Uldae-ri, Jangheung-myeon, Yangju City, prompting an immediate evacuation order. Nearby Hunters and military units are working together to suppress it, and six casualties have been confirmed so far…

[P168]
“Goddamn it. As if the traffic wasn’t bad enough, now those monster bastards are raising hell too.”

[P169]
After delivering the colorful curse, he glanced at me in the passenger seat.

[P170]
“You’re a Hunter too, right?”

[P171]
“For now.”

[P172]
At this point, I wasn’t entirely sure whether I was a Hunter or a Murim warrior.

[P173]
Officially, at least in the modern world, I was a C-rank Hunter with Hope Guild.

[P174]
The taxi driver grinned at my answer.

[P175]
“I knew it. You can always spot a Hunter.”

[P176]
“I suppose so.”

[P177]
It was like the difference between a herbivore and a carnivore.

[P178]
There were exceptions, but everyone gave off a certain air. Someone my size carrying a large case had to be one of two things:

[P179]
A musician who loved working out, or a Hunter.

[P180]
*You can tell at a glance.*

[P181]
It wasn’t anything particularly remarkable, especially for a taxi driver who met countless passengers every day.

[P182]
But this middle-aged man’s mouth never stopped moving.

[P183]
“Hey, can I ask you something?”

[P184]
“Sure.”

[P185]
“It feels like Gates have been opening more often lately. Can’t anything be done about that?”

[P186]
“……What?”

[P187]
“I mean, how are ordinary people like me supposed to live without worrying? I could wake up tomorrow morning and find a Gate in my apartment parking lot. I can work my ass off taking fares all day, but it’s not like I can afford property in a safe zone.”

[P188]
I stared at him incredulously.

[P189]
“That’s true, but why are you asking me?”

[P190]
“I know. I’m just frustrated, that’s all. Frustrated.”

[P191]
“……So am I.”

[P192]
I was a Hunter, not a prophet.

[P193]
How was I supposed to predict something even Nostradamus couldn’t?

[P194]
No one could predict when or where a Gate would form. The only reason early suppression was possible was because astronomical sums had been spent installing mana detectors everywhere.

[P195]
Just like the breaking news now coming over the radio.

[P196]
> Breaking news. The F-rank Gate reported earlier in Yangju City has been stabilized. Hunters and military forces have exterminated a total of fifty-eight goblins and are conducting a search for any remaining monsters…

[P197]
“Every time you turn around, it’s Gates and monsters. I’m sick to death of it.”

[P198]
Beep.

[P199]
The taxi driver switched off the radio with an irritated jab.

[P200]
An uncomfortable silence settled over the car, but I was more than happy to spend the rest of the trip in peace.

[P201]
*I wonder what Mom and Hayeon are doing right now.*

[P202]
I was gazing out the window, lost in thought, when it happened.

[P203]
Honk! Hoooonk!

[P204]
A faint blare pierced my ears, followed by a jumble of overlapping noises. I hurriedly rolled down the window.

[P205]
*What is that? Was there an accident?*

[P206]
The taxi driver stared at me in confusion.

[P207]
“Why are you opening the window when I’ve got the air conditioner on—”

[P208]
“Wait. Just give me a second.”

[P209]
My serious tone silenced him. I drew up my internal energy.

[P210]
My hearing and vision, already far beyond the limits of an ordinary human, swept across the congested road.

[P211]
“Huh?”

[P212]
Far in the distance, a black dot shot into the air.

[P213]
It began to fall in an arc, and I realized what it was.

[P214]
“……A car?”

[P215]
It had been crushed into a ball, but I could still see it clearly.

[P216]
The crumpled hood. The twisted metal.

[P217]
The shower of glass spilling from it as it hurtled toward us.

[P218]
And exactly where it was going to land.

[P219]
Whoooooosh!

[P220]
*Oh, shit.*

[P221]
Why here of all places?
